scope.note: A 1,000-card deck showing 10 examples each, to read the harvest by eye and to see how v10 does on it. Ranks 1-1000 sit at harvest budget 80, so 10 displayed examples draw from a pool eight times that size.

inventory.source_note: Counts come from subtitles because the app teaches speech and the harvest reads subtitles; CNK SYN2015 is written Czech and ranks newspaper vocabulary first. CNK is not discarded -- it corroborates every surface, supplies the capitalisation evidence that removes proper nouns, and enriches lemma/POS afterwards via svk-lookup at 99.9% coverage. See the snapshot's snapshot.json.

harvest.source_note: Tatoeba first, OpenSubtitles for the tail. Tatoeba sentences are human-written and clean; Czech OpenSubtitles carries a lot of amateur translation, of which roughly 8% of displayed examples were broken or calqued from English. Tatoeba reaches 5 matches on 87% of these 3000 cards and none at all on 149, so it cannot serve the tail alone.
harvest.budget_note: Headroom, not a display count. The harvest exists to let a sense distribution be estimated later from about 10 scored occurrences, and WSD will skip some of those, so the pool must hold well more than 10. Floor is 30 at the tail -- twice the 15 a card should almost always have, three times the 10 to be scored. Retaining more costs disk and nothing else: what reaches WSD is governed by execution_cap_per_card. This is the number that cannot be raised later without harvesting again.

wsd.occurrence_pos_note: Czech declares no occurrence POS: spaCy publishes no Czech pipeline, and a POS filter can only subtract candidates, so an unvalidated one deletes correct senses. See cs-v10-1.
